name: Mount Everest
description: Highest peak in the world and the most iconic mountaineering objective on Earth. First summited by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953.
closestAirportDistance: 140 km by road to Lukla, then trek to Base Camp
permitInfo: Nepal Mountaineering Association permit required; royalty fee of $11,000 per climber for standard route. Liaison officer required.

name: K2
description: Second highest peak in the world, widely considered the most difficult and dangerous 8000m peak to climb. Known as the 'Savage Mountain'.
closestAirportDistance: 620 km by road to Skardu, then trek to Base Camp
permitInfo: Pakistan Alpine Club permit required; approximately $7,200 per climber plus peak fee. Liaison officer and environmental bond required.

name: Kangchenjunga
description: Third highest peak in the world, straddling the border of Nepal and Sikkim, India. Revered as sacred by the local Sikkimese people.
closestAirportDistance: Flight to Bhadrapur then drive and trek, approx 2 weeks approach
permitInfo: Nepal Mountaineering Association permit required; royalty fee applies. Climbers traditionally stop short of the true summit out of respect for local beliefs.

name: Lhotse
description: Fourth highest peak in the world, connected to Everest via the South Col. Its south face is one of the steepest walls in the Himalayas.
closestAirportDistance: 140 km by road to Lukla, then trek to Base Camp
permitInfo: Nepal Mountaineering Association permit required; shares Everest Base Camp approach. Royalty fee of approximately $10,000 per climber.

name: Makalu
description: Fifth highest peak in the world, known for its striking pyramid shape. Located about 19 km southeast of Mount Everest.
closestAirportDistance: Flight to Tumlingtar then multi-day trek to Base Camp
permitInfo: Nepal Mountaineering Association permit required; royalty fee applies. Remote approach adds logistical complexity.

name: Cho Oyu
description: Sixth highest peak in the world and considered the easiest 8000m peak to climb. Located in the Khumbu region west of Everest.
closestAirportDistance: Drive to Tingri (Tibet side) or trek from Namche (Nepal side)
permitInfo: Nepal or China/Tibet Mountaineering Association permit required depending on route. Royalty fee applies.

name: Dhaulagiri
description: Seventh highest peak in the world, whose name means 'White Mountain' in Sanskrit. It was the highest known peak until Kangchenjunga was discovered.

name: Manaslu
description: Eighth highest peak in the world, also known as the 'Mountain of the Spirit'. First climbed by a Japanese expedition in 1956.

name: Nanga Parbat
description: Ninth highest peak in the world, known as the 'Killer Mountain' due to its high fatality rate. Features the massive Rupal Face, one of the highest rock walls on Earth.

name: Annapurna I
description: Tenth highest peak in the world and the first 8000m peak ever climbed, summited by Maurice Herzog in 1950. It has the highest fatality-to-summit ratio of any 8000er.

name: Gasherbrum I
description: Eleventh highest peak in the world, also known as Hidden Peak. Located in the Gasherbrum massif of the Karakoram range.

name: Broad Peak
description: Twelfth highest peak in the world, named for its broad summit ridge over 1.5 km long. Located near K2 on the China-Pakistan border.

name: Gasherbrum II
description: Thirteenth highest peak in the world, considered one of the easier 8000m peaks. Located in the Gasherbrum massif of the Karakoram.

name: Shishapangma
description: Fourteenth highest peak in the world and the lowest of the 8000m peaks. The last 8000er to be climbed, summited in 1964 by a Chinese expedition.

name: Denali
description: Highest peak in North America and one of the Seven Summits. Known for extreme cold and severe weather, it has the largest base-to-summit rise of any mountain on Earth.

name: Aconcagua
description: Highest peak in South America, the Western Hemisphere, and the Southern Hemisphere. One of the Seven Summits and a popular high-altitude mountaineering objective.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: Highest peak in Africa and one of the Seven Summits. A free-standing volcanic mountain and the highest single free-standing mountain above base in the world.

name: Mount Elbrus
description: Highest peak in Europe (by the common continental boundary definition) and one of the Seven Summits. A dormant stratovolcano with twin summits.

name: Mount Vinson
description: Highest peak in Antarctica and one of the Seven Summits. Located about 1,200 km from the South Pole in the Ellsworth Mountains.

name: Puncak Jaya
description: Highest peak in Oceania and one of the Seven Summits (Messner list). Features a challenging rock climbing route on its limestone summit pyramid.

name: Mount Kosciuszko
description: Highest peak on the Australian mainland and one of the Seven Summits (Bass list). A gentle walk to the summit makes it the easiest of the Seven Summits.

name: Mont Blanc
description: Highest peak in the Alps and Western Europe. A premier mountaineering destination and the birthplace of modern alpinism.

name: Matterhorn
description: One of the most iconic and recognizable mountains in the world with its distinctive pyramidal shape. First ascended in 1865 by Edward Whymper.

name: Eiger
description: Famous for its dramatic North Face (Nordwand), one of the great north faces of the Alps. The Eiger North Face has a storied and tragic climbing history.

name: Jungfrau
description: One of the main summits of the Bernese Alps, forming a prominent trio with the Eiger and Monch. Home to the highest railway station in Europe.

name: Monte Rosa
description: Second highest peak in the Alps and the highest in Switzerland. The Dufourspitze is the culmination of the Monte Rosa massif.

name: Dom
description: Third highest peak in the Alps and the highest mountain entirely within Switzerland. Part of the Mischabel group in the Pennine Alps.

name: Weisshorn
description: One of the most majestic peaks in the Alps, known for its elegant pyramidal shape. Considered one of the finest mountaineering objectives in the Pennine Alps.

name: Gran Paradiso
description: Highest peak entirely within Italy and the centerpiece of Gran Paradiso National Park. A popular mountaineering summit in the Graian Alps.

name: Grossglockner
description: Highest mountain in Austria, located in the Hohe Tauern range. A classic alpine climb with glacier approaches and a dramatic summit ridge.

name: Zugspitze
description: Highest peak in Germany, located on the Austrian border in the Wetterstein Mountains. Accessible by cable car and cog railway.

name: Mount Rainier
description: Highest peak in the Cascade Range and the most glaciated peak in the contiguous United States. An active stratovolcano and iconic Pacific Northwest landmark.

name: Mount Hood
description: Highest peak in Oregon and one of the most climbed glaciated peaks in the world. An active stratovolcano with year-round skiing on Palmer Glacier.

name: Mount Shasta
description: Prominent stratovolcano in Northern California and the second highest peak in the Cascades. Known for its dramatic rise above the surrounding terrain.

name: Mount Adams
description: Second highest peak in Washington state and a large stratovolcano in the Cascade Range. Known for its massive glacial coverage and volcanic features.

name: Mount Baker
description: Active glaciated stratovolcano in the North Cascades of Washington. Holds the world record for the most snowfall in a single season (1998-99).

name: Mount Whitney
description: Highest peak in the contiguous United States at 14,505 feet. Located on the boundary of Sequoia National Park and Inyo National Forest.

name: Mount Williamson
description: Second highest peak in the Sierra Nevada and California. A remote and rugged peak requiring significant cross-country travel to reach.

name: Half Dome
description: Iconic granite dome in Yosemite National Park, famous for its sheer northwest face. The Regular Northwest Face route is a classic big wall rock climb.

name: El Capitan
description: Iconic 3,000-foot granite monolith in Yosemite Valley, considered the center of the big wall climbing world. The Nose route is one of the most famous rock climbs on Earth.

name: Mount Foraker
description: Second highest peak in the Alaska Range and a formidable mountaineering objective. Known for its long, committing routes and severe weather.

name: Mount Hunter
description: Major peak in the Alaska Range near Denali, known for its steep and technical climbing routes. The Moonflower Buttress is a legendary alpine route.

name: Mount Saint Elias
description: Second highest peak in both the United States and Canada. One of the most dramatic rises from sea level of any mountain in the world.

name: Mount Bona
description: Highest volcano in the Saint Elias Mountains and one of the highest peaks in North America. A remote and heavily glaciated peak in Wrangell-St. Elias.

name: Mount Blackburn
description: Highest peak in the Wrangell Mountains and fifth highest in the United States. A massive volcanic peak in Wrangell-St. Elias National Park.

name: Mount Sanford
description: A massive shield volcano in the Wrangell Mountains of Alaska. One of the highest volcanoes in North America.

name: Mount Fairweather
description: Highest peak in British Columbia and the Fairweather Range, straddling the Alaska-Canada border. Located near Glacier Bay National Park.

name: Mount Logan
description: Highest peak in Canada and second highest in North America. Has the largest base circumference of any non-volcanic mountain on Earth.

name: Ojos del Salado
description: Highest volcano in the world and second highest peak in the Andes and the Western Hemisphere. Located on the Argentina-Chile border in the Atacama region.

name: Huascaran
description: Highest peak in Peru and the Cordillera Blanca. Site of a devastating 1970 avalanche triggered by an earthquake that killed thousands.

name: Chimborazo
description: Highest peak in Ecuador and the point on Earth's surface farthest from the center of the Earth due to the equatorial bulge. An inactive stratovolcano.

name: Cotopaxi
description: One of the highest active volcanoes in the world and a classic glacier climb in Ecuador. Known for its near-perfect conical shape.

name: Illimani
description: Highest peak in the Cordillera Real of Bolivia, towering over the city of La Paz. A prominent four-peaked massif visible from the Altiplano.

name: Sajama
description: Highest peak in Bolivia, a dormant stratovolcano in Sajama National Park. Known for its high-altitude grasslands and the world's highest forest.

name: Alpamayo
description: Stunning ice peak in the Cordillera Blanca once voted the most beautiful mountain in the world. Known for its near-perfect pyramidal summit of ice.

name: Fitz Roy
description: Iconic granite spire in Patagonia, known for extremely challenging technical climbing and notoriously bad weather. Inspiration for the Patagonia clothing brand logo.

name: Cerro Torre
description: One of the most spectacular and difficult peaks in the world, a slender granite tower capped by an ice mushroom. Its first ascent is one of mountaineering's great controversies.

name: Mount Elbert
description: Highest peak in Colorado and the Rocky Mountains at 14,440 feet. Located in the Sawatch Range near Leadville.

name: Mount Massive
description: Second highest peak in Colorado at 14,428 feet, with the most area above 14,000 feet of any peak in the contiguous US. Located in the Sawatch Range.

name: Mount Harvard
description: Third highest peak in Colorado at 14,421 feet, in the Collegiate Peaks of the Sawatch Range. Named for Harvard University.

name: Blanca Peak
description: Fourth highest peak in Colorado at 14,351 feet and highpoint of the Sangre de Cristo Range. Sacred to the Navajo as the eastern boundary of their homeland.

name: La Plata Peak
description: Fifth highest peak in Colorado at 14,343 feet, located in the Sawatch Range. A popular but sometimes underestimated fourteener.

name: Uncompahgre Peak
description: Sixth highest peak in Colorado at 14,321 feet and highest in the San Juan Mountains. Features a distinctive flat-topped summit.

name: Crestone Peak
description: Seventh highest peak in Colorado at 14,300 feet, in the Sangre de Cristo Range. One of the most challenging Colorado fourteeners to climb.

name: Mount Lincoln
description: Eighth highest peak in Colorado at 14,293 feet, located in the Mosquito Range. Often combined with neighboring fourteeners Democrat, Cameron, and Bross.

name: Grays Peak
description: Highest point on the Continental Divide in North America at 14,278 feet. Often climbed together with neighboring Torreys Peak.

name: Mount Antero
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,276 feet in the Sawatch Range. Famous for its aquamarine gemstone deposits found near the summit.

name: Torreys Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,275 feet, located on the Continental Divide in the Front Range. Almost always climbed together with neighboring Grays Peak.

name: Castle Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,279 feet, highest peak in the Elk Mountains. Known for its rugged terrain and scenic location near Aspen.

name: Quandary Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,271 feet in the Tenmile Range. One of the most accessible and popular fourteeners near Breckenridge.

name: Mount Evans
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,271 feet in the Front Range, accessible by the highest paved road in North America. Renamed Mount Blue Sky in 2023.

name: Longs Peak
description: Iconic Colorado fourteener at 14,259 feet in Rocky Mountain National Park. The Keyhole Route and the Diamond face are famous climbing objectives.

name: Mount Wilson
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,252 feet in the San Miguel Mountains near Telluride. A challenging peak with significant exposure on the standard route.

name: Mount Cameron
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,239 feet in the Mosquito Range, though some lists dispute its status due to low prominence. Often combined with Lincoln, Democrat, and Bross.

name: Mount Shavano
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,231 feet in the Sawatch Range. Named after Ute Chief Shavano and often climbed with neighboring Tabeguache Peak.

name: Mount Belford
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,203 feet in the Sawatch Range. Often combined with nearby Mount Oxford and Missouri Mountain.

name: Crestone Needle
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,203 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. One of the most technical standard routes of any fourteener, requiring Class 3 scrambling.

name: Mount Princeton
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,204 feet in the Collegiate Peaks of the Sawatch Range. Known for hot springs at its base near Buena Vista.

name: Mount Yale
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,200 feet in the Collegiate Peaks of the Sawatch Range. Named for Yale University and featuring a scenic climb from Denny Creek.

name: Mount Bross
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,178 feet in the Mosquito Range. Often climbed as part of the Decalibron loop with Democrat, Cameron, and Lincoln.

name: Kit Carson Mountain
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,167 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. A challenging peak often combined with Challenger Point.

name: El Diente Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,165 feet in the San Miguel Mountains. The traverse from Mount Wilson to El Diente is one of the classic Colorado ridge traverses.

name: Maroon Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,163 feet, the higher of the Maroon Bells near Aspen. Known as one of the 'Deadly Bells' due to its crumbly sedimentary rock.

name: Tabeguache Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,162 feet in the Sawatch Range. Almost always climbed together with Mount Shavano via a connecting ridge.

name: Mount Oxford
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,160 feet in the Sawatch Range. Often combined with Mount Belford on a popular day hike.

name: Mount Sneffels
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,158 feet in the San Juan Mountains. One of the most photographed peaks in Colorado with a striking profile.

name: Mount Democrat
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,155 feet in the Mosquito Range. Part of the popular Decalibron loop combining four fourteeners in one day.

name: Capitol Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,137 feet in the Elk Mountains. Considered one of the most difficult and dangerous fourteeners due to its exposed Knife Edge ridge.

name: Pikes Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,115 feet, perhaps the most famous peak in Colorado. Inspired 'America the Beautiful' and is accessible by highway and cog railway.

name: Snowmass Mountain
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,099 feet in the Elk Mountains. Known for its remote approach and challenging route on loose rock.

name: Mount Eolus
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,090 feet in the Weminuche Wilderness. Accessed via the Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad.

name: Windom Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,087 feet in the Needle Mountains of the San Juans. Often combined with Sunlight Peak and Mount Eolus.

name: Challenger Point
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,087 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. Named in memory of the Space Shuttle Challenger crew and often combined with Kit Carson.

name: Mount Columbia
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,077 feet in the Collegiate Peaks of the Sawatch Range. One of the more remote fourteeners requiring a long approach.

name: Missouri Mountain
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,074 feet in the Sawatch Range. Features a scenic approach through Missouri Gulch and is often combined with Belford and Oxford.

name: Humboldt Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,064 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. One of the easier fourteeners in the range with a straightforward hiking route.

name: Mount Bierstadt
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,065 feet in the Front Range. One of the most popular and accessible fourteeners, often a hiker's first fourteener.

name: Sunlight Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,063 feet in the Needle Mountains. Features an exposed summit block requiring careful Class 4 climbing.

name: Handies Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,053 feet in the San Juan Mountains. One of the easiest fourteeners with a relatively short hike from the trailhead.

name: Culebra Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,053 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. Located on private land requiring a fee for access, making it one of the least climbed fourteeners.

name: North Maroon Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,019 feet, the lower of the Maroon Bells. The traverse between Maroon and North Maroon is one of the most dangerous fourteener routes.

name: Mount Lindsey
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,048 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. Features a scenic approach and a fun Class 3 gully on the standard route.

name: Little Bear Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,043 feet in the Sangre de Cristo Range. Considered one of the most difficult fourteeners with Class 4 climbing and significant rockfall hazard.

name: Mount Sherman
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,043 feet in the Mosquito Range. One of the easiest fourteeners with a gentle hiking trail past old mining ruins.

name: Redcloud Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,040 feet in the San Juan Mountains. Named for the reddish rock near the summit, often climbed with neighboring Sunshine Peak.

name: Pyramid Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,025 feet in the Elk Mountains near Aspen. A challenging peak with loose rock and steep couloirs.

name: Wilson Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,018 feet in the San Miguel Mountains. The peak depicted on the Coors beer logo, located near Telluride.

name: Wetterhorn Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,019 feet in the San Juan Mountains. Features a dramatic summit block requiring exposed Class 3 scrambling.

name: San Luis Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,022 feet, the most remote fourteener in Colorado. The only fourteener in the La Garita Wilderness.

name: Sunshine Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,004 feet in the San Juan Mountains. Almost always climbed in combination with neighboring Redcloud Peak.

name: Mount of the Holy Cross
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,011 feet in the Sawatch Range. Famous for the snow-filled cross-shaped couloir on its northeast face.

name: Huron Peak
description: Colorado fourteener at 14,010 feet in the Sawatch Range. A scenic and relatively straightforward climb from the South Winfield trailhead.

name: Mount Olympus
description: Highest peak in Greece and mythological home of the Greek gods. Mytikas is the highest of several summit pinnacles.

name: Mount Fuji
description: Highest peak in Japan and one of the most iconic mountains in the world. An active stratovolcano and UNESCO World Heritage Site climbed by hundreds of thousands annually.

name: Mount Cook
description: Highest peak in New Zealand and a major mountaineering destination in the Southern Alps. Where Sir Edmund Hillary honed his climbing skills before Everest.

name: Mount Blanc du Tacul
description: Major peak in the Mont Blanc massif on the standard Three Monts route to the summit of Mont Blanc. Popular ice climbing destination.

name: Dent Blanche
description: Prominent peak in the Pennine Alps known for its imposing appearance and challenging climbing routes. One of the classic 4000m peaks of the Alps.

name: Aiguille Verte
description: Major peak in the Mont Blanc massif, considered a serious mountaineering objective. The Whymper Couloir and the Couturier Couloir are famous alpine routes.

name: Grandes Jorasses
description: Major peak in the Mont Blanc massif, renowned for its north face which is one of the three great north faces of the Alps. The Walker Spur is a legendary route.

name: Mount Kenya
description: Second highest peak in Africa, an extinct stratovolcano with dramatic rock spires. Batian is the highest point, requiring technical rock climbing.

name: Mount Stanley
description: Third highest peak in Africa and highest in the Rwenzori Mountains, known as the 'Mountains of the Moon'. Features equatorial glaciers and lush alpine vegetation.

name: Mount Erebus
description: The southernmost active volcano on Earth, located on Ross Island in Antarctica. Contains a persistent lava lake in its summit crater.

name: Ama Dablam
description: One of the most visually striking peaks in the Himalayas, often called the 'Matterhorn of the Himalayas'. A popular and technically challenging climbing objective.

name: Island Peak
description: Popular trekking peak in the Everest region of Nepal. One of the most climbed peaks in the Himalayas, offering an accessible introduction to high-altitude mountaineering.

name: Pumori
description: Striking peak visible from Everest Base Camp, sometimes called 'Daughter Peak' as it was named by Mallory after his daughter. A challenging 7000m objective.

name: Nuptse
description: Seventh highest mountain in the world by some rankings, forming the western wall of the Everest amphitheater. Its south face is one of the greatest walls in the Himalayas.

name: Annapurna III
description: Major peak in the Annapurna massif, notable for having a very challenging south face. One of the more difficult 7000m peaks in Nepal.

name: Masherbrum
description: Striking peak in the Karakoram, originally designated K1 in the Great Trigonometric Survey. Known for its dramatic twin summits and challenging climbing.

name: Mount Blanc de Courmayeur
description: Secondary summit of the Mont Blanc massif, the highest point entirely within Italy. Located on the Italian ridge of Mont Blanc.

name: Lyskamm
description: Major peak in the Monte Rosa massif, known as the 'Man-Eater' due to its dangerous corniced ridge. A classic but serious alpine traverse.

name: Mount Robson
description: Highest peak in the Canadian Rockies, known as the 'Monarch of the Canadian Rockies'. A formidable mountaineering objective with notoriously poor weather.

name: Mount Columbia (Canada)
description: Highest peak in Alberta and the second highest in the Canadian Rockies. Located on the Columbia Icefield, the largest ice field in the Rocky Mountains.

name: Grand Teton
description: Highest peak in the Teton Range and one of the most iconic climbing peaks in North America. Rising dramatically above the valley floor of Jackson Hole.

name: Gannett Peak
description: Highest peak in Wyoming, located in the remote Wind River Range. Requires a long approach through the Bridger Wilderness to reach.

name: Mount Mitchell
description: Highest peak east of the Mississippi River and highest in the Appalachian Mountains. Located in Mount Mitchell State Park on the Blue Ridge Parkway.

name: Mount Washington
description: Highest peak in the northeastern United States, notorious for its extreme weather. Once held the world record for highest wind speed recorded at a surface station.

name: Mount Katahdin
description: Highest peak in Maine and the northern terminus of the Appalachian Trail. A dramatic granite massif featuring the famous Knife Edge ridge traverse.

name: Mauna Kea
description: Highest point in Hawaii and technically the tallest mountain on Earth when measured from its oceanic base. Home to major astronomical observatories.

name: Mauna Loa
description: The largest active volcano on Earth by volume and area. Located on the Big Island of Hawaii, it last erupted in 2022.

name: Wheeler Peak
description: Highest peak in New Mexico, located in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains near Taos. A popular day hike with above-treeline alpine terrain.

name: Humphreys Peak
description: Highest point in Arizona, an eroded stratovolcano in the San Francisco Peaks near Flagstaff. Sacred to several Native American tribes.

name: Borah Peak
description: Highest peak in Idaho, located in the Lost River Range. Features a challenging scramble along a narrow ridge known as Chicken Out Ridge.

name: Kings Peak
description: Highest peak in Utah, located in the Uinta Mountains of the Ashley National Forest. Requires a long backpacking approach through the High Uintas Wilderness.

name: Granite Peak
description: Highest peak in Montana, located in the Beartooth Range of the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness. One of the most difficult US state highpoints to reach.

name: Cloud Peak
description: Highest peak in the Bighorn Mountains and Cloud Peak Wilderness. A remote peak requiring a multi-day backpacking approach across alpine terrain.

name: Guadalupe Peak
description: Highest point in Texas, located in Guadalupe Mountains National Park. A well-maintained trail leads to the summit with expansive desert views.

name: Mount Marcy
description: Highest point in New York State, located in the Adirondack High Peaks region. The source of the Hudson River is Lake Tear of the Clouds on its slopes.

name: Clingmans Dome
description: Highest point in Tennessee and the Great Smoky Mountains. Features a distinctive observation tower at the summit, accessible by a paved trail.

name: Triglav
description: Highest peak in Slovenia and the Julian Alps, featured on the Slovenian national flag and coat of arms. A national symbol and popular climbing destination.

name: Kazbek
description: Third highest peak in the Caucasus and a prominent stratovolcano. Steeped in mythology and one of the most popular mountaineering objectives in the region.

name: Mount Ararat
description: Highest peak in Turkey, a dormant compound volcano traditionally associated with the biblical Noah's Ark. Symbolically important to the Armenian people.

name: Mount Damavand
description: Highest volcano in Asia and highest peak in Iran. A stratovolcano with fumaroles near the summit, prominent in Persian mythology.

name: Mount Kinabalu
description: Highest peak in Borneo and Malaysia. A UNESCO World Heritage Site known for exceptional biodiversity and the Via Ferrata climbing route.

name: Mount Tyree
description: Second highest peak in Antarctica, located near Mount Vinson. One of the least climbed major peaks in the world due to its remote Antarctic location.

name: Pico de Orizaba
description: Highest peak in Mexico and third highest in North America. A dormant stratovolcano with a glaciated summit, popular for mountaineering.

name: Iztaccihuatl
description: Third highest peak in Mexico, a dormant volcano whose ridgeline resembles a sleeping woman. Part of an Aztec legend paired with neighboring Popocatepetl.

name: Popocatepetl
description: Second highest peak in Mexico and one of the most active volcanoes in the country. Currently off-limits to climbers due to ongoing volcanic activity.

name: Aiguille du Midi
description: Iconic peak above Chamonix accessible by cable car, serving as the starting point for the Mont Blanc ascent and the Vallee Blanche ski descent.

name: Mount Hua
description: One of China's Five Great Mountains, famous for its steep and narrow plank paths. Known as one of the most dangerous hikes in the world.

name: Toubkal
description: Highest peak in North Africa and the Atlas Mountains. A popular trekking destination accessible from Marrakech.

name: Teide
description: Highest peak in Spain and the Atlantic Islands, a massive stratovolcano on the island of Tenerife. The third tallest volcanic structure in the world.

name: Mount Aspiring
description: Often called the 'Matterhorn of the South' due to its pyramidal shape. The highest peak outside the Aoraki/Mount Cook region of the Southern Alps.

name: Devils Tower
description: Iconic igneous intrusion and America's first national monument. A world-famous rock climbing destination with hundreds of parallel crack routes on its columnar basalt.

name: Shiprock
description: Dramatic volcanic neck rising above the New Mexico desert, sacred to the Navajo people. Climbing has been banned since 1970 at the request of the Navajo Nation.

name: Mount Waddington
description: Highest peak entirely within British Columbia and the highest in the Coast Mountains. A remote and challenging peak requiring technical climbing skills.

name: Mount Sir Donald
description: Prominent peak in Glacier National Park of Canada. Its classic Northwest Arete is considered one of the finest alpine rock climbs in the Canadian Rockies.

name: Bugaboo Spire
description: Iconic granite tower in the Bugaboo Group, one of North America's premier alpine rock climbing destinations. The Northeast Ridge is a legendary alpine route.

name: Cerro Aconcagua
description: The south summit of Aconcagua, slightly lower than the main peak. Part of the massive Aconcagua massif in the Andes of Argentina.

name: Nevado Huascaran Norte
description: Northern summit of the Huascaran massif in the Cordillera Blanca. Connected to the main summit by a high saddle.

name: Mercedario
description: Sixth highest peak in the Andes and highest in the San Juan province of Argentina. A remote and seldom-climbed peak in the high Andes.

name: Nevado de Cachi
description: Prominent peak in the Andes of northwestern Argentina. A relatively accessible high Andean peak near the town of Cachi in Salta province.

name: Tres Cruces
description: Major Andean peak on the Argentina-Chile border. One of the highest peaks in the Puna de Atacama region.

name: Pissis
description: Third highest peak in the Western Hemisphere and highest dormant volcano in the world. Located in the remote Puna de Atacama region.

name: Bonete
description: Major Andean peak in northwestern Argentina. One of the highest peaks in the Americas, located in the remote Puna de Atacama.

name: Mount Shuksan
description: Spectacularly beautiful peak in the North Cascades, frequently photographed from Picture Lake. A classic alpine climbing objective with multiple routes.

name: Mount Olympus (Washington)
description: Highest peak in the Olympic Mountains and centerpiece of Olympic National Park. Home to some of the lowest elevation glaciers in the contiguous US.

name: Mount Stuart
description: Second highest non-volcanic peak in Washington and a massive granite batholith. The North Ridge is one of the finest alpine rock routes in the Cascades.

name: Glacier Peak
description: Most remote of Washington's major volcanic peaks, located deep in the Glacier Peak Wilderness. A heavily glaciated stratovolcano.

name: Mount Blanc de Cheilon
description: Prominent peak in the Pennine Alps of Switzerland. A challenging alpine peak above the Lac des Dix and the Grande Dixence Dam.

name: Breithorn
description: One of the easiest 4000m peaks in the Alps, accessible from the Klein Matterhorn cable car. Popular as a first 4000m summit experience.

name: Castor
description: Peak in the Monte Rosa massif named after one of the twins in Greek mythology. Often climbed together with its twin peak Pollux.

name: Schreckhorn
description: Highest peak of the Bernese Alps that is not on the main watershed divide. Known for its dramatic appearance and serious mountaineering routes.

name: Monch
description: Central peak of the famous Eiger-Monch-Jungfrau trio in the Bernese Oberland. The Southeast Ridge is a popular introduction to alpine climbing.

name: Piz Bernina
description: The highest peak in the Eastern Alps and the only 4000m peak east of the Bernese Alps. Famous for the spectacular Biancograt (white ridge) snow arete.

name: Ben Nevis
description: The highest peak in the British Isles. Home to some of the finest winter climbing in Scotland on its dramatic north face. The summit held the former world record for wind speed.
